correctness.rationale: The bipartite max-flow/min-cut criterion identifies the edge polytope exactly with x,y>=0, each sum=1, x_i+y_i<=1. Bipartite incidence total unimodularity proves integral normality. At a vertex only two of the diagonal facets can be active; an exhaustive case split shows the maximal nonsmooth faces are row stars, column stars, or reverse-edge segments, and checks smoothness for the other faces by an integral primitive basis. All those maximal cones have one primitive ray dependence, hence are singular. Quotienting the saturated tangent semigroups gives rank-one 2-by-(n-1) or 2-by-(2n-4) determinantal transverse cones; their Segre degrees give exact multiplicities. The corresponding orbit closures are linear coordinate spaces, with explicit support intersections. Deterministic exhaustive face/Smith-normal-form checks for n=3 through n=6 reproduce the singular-face down-closures and no omitted nonunimodular simplicial cases; finite checking is corroboration, not proof for arbitrary n.

value.rationale: The crown graph edge variety is a natural diagonal-free projection of the Segre embedding and canonical algebraic-statistics structural-zero model. Its full reduced singular support has two large families of coordinate projective (n-2)-spaces and a further binomial(n,2) singular lines, an unexpected lower-dimensional family for n>=4. The two inequivalent rank-one local models and multiplicities n-1 and 2n-4, and the sharp n=3 equidimensional transition, are precise invariants useful for studying toric degenerations, intersection theory and local geometry. These facts are not routine numerical restatements of the prior Hilbert numerator; the classification requires global face exhaustion and saturated local semigroup analysis.
